title: One-way ANOVA F-stat
context: Compare group means with ANOVA (even for two groups).
task: Set result to the F-statistic of a one-way ANOVA on value across groups A and B, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value']
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value']
result = round(float(stats.f_oneway(A, B).statistic), 3)

title: ANOVA vs t-test equivalence
context: For two groups, F = t². Verify.
task: Set result to the ANOVA F-statistic minus the squared t-statistic (equal-var t-test) for groups A and B — should be ~0, rounded to 4 decimals.
answer:
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value']
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value']
f = stats.f_oneway(A, B).statistic
t = stats.ttest_ind(A, B).statistic
result = round(float(f - t ** 2), 4)

title: Bootstrap CI lower bound
task: Using a fixed seed np.random.seed(0), draw 2000 bootstrap resamples (with replacement) of sample x, take each mean, and set result to the 2.5th percentile of those means, rounded to 2 decimals.
answer:
np.random.seed(0)
x = sample['x'].to_numpy()
means = [np.random.choice(x, size=len(x), replace=True).mean() for _ in range(2000)]
result = round(float(np.percentile(means, 2.5)), 2)

title: Bootstrap standard error
context: SE of the mean via resampling.
task: With np.random.seed(0) and 2000 bootstrap resamples of sample x, set result to the standard deviation of the resample means (ddof=0), rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
np.random.seed(0)
x = sample['x'].to_numpy()
means = [np.random.choice(x, size=len(x), replace=True).mean() for _ in range(2000)]
result = round(float(np.std(means)), 3)

title: Monte Carlo probability
task: With np.random.seed(1), simulate 100000 rolls of two fair dice and set result to the fraction summing to 7, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
np.random.seed(1)
rolls = np.random.randint(1, 7, size=(100000, 2)).sum(axis=1)
result = round(float((rolls == 7).mean()), 3)

title: Standardised effect for power
task: Set result to Cohen's d for the paired improvement = mean(after−before) / std(after−before, ddof=1), rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
d = paired['after'] - paired['before']
result = round(float(d.mean() / d.std()), 3)

title: Slope from covariance
task: Set result to the regression slope of score on hours computed as cov(hours,score)/var(hours) (ddof=1), rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
c = np.cov(regression['hours'], regression['score'])
result = round(float(c[0, 1] / c[0, 0]), 3)

title: Residual standard error
context: Spread of residuals about the line.
task: Set result to the residual standard error = sqrt(SSE / (n−2)) for score on hours, rounded to 3 decimals.
hint: SSE = sum of squared residuals; n-2 df.
answer:
r = stats.linregress(regression['hours'], regression['score'])
pred = r.slope * regression['hours'] + r.intercept
sse = ((regression['score'] - pred) ** 2).sum()
result = round(float(np.sqrt(sse / (len(regression) - 2))), 3)

title: Standardised coefficient
context: Slope in SD units equals correlation.
task: Set result to the standardised regression coefficient of score on hours = slope * std(hours)/std(score) (ddof=1), rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
r = stats.linregress(regression['hours'], regression['score'])
beta = r.slope * regression['hours'].std() / regression['score'].std()
result = round(float(beta), 3)

title: Sampling distribution of the mean
task: With np.random.seed(2), draw 5000 samples of size 30 from sample x (with replacement), and set result to the std (ddof=0) of their means, rounded to 3 decimals.

x = sample['x'].to_numpy()

title: Goodness-of-fit test
task: For observed counts [18, 22, 16, 24, 20, 20] across six die faces, set result to the chi-square goodness-of-fit p-value against a uniform expectation, rounded to 4 decimals.
answer:
obs = [18, 22, 16, 24, 20, 20]

title: Pooled z for two proportions
task: Set result to the pooled two-proportion z-statistic for treatment vs control conversions, rounded to 3 decimals. Use the pooled proportion for the standard error.
answer:
e = experiment.set_index('variant')
xc, nc = e.loc['control', 'conversions'], e.loc['control', 'visitors']
xt, nt = e.loc['treatment', 'conversions'], e.loc['treatment', 'visitors']
pc, pt = xc / nc, xt / nt
pp = (xc + xt) / (nc + nt)
se = np.sqrt(pp * (1 - pp) * (1 / nc + 1 / nt))
result = round(float((pt - pc) / se), 3)

title: Two-proportion p-value
task: Set result to the two-sided p-value from the pooled two-proportion z-test (treatment vs control), rounded to 4 decimals.
answer:
e = experiment.set_index('variant')
xc, nc = e.loc['control', 'conversions'], e.loc['control', 'visitors']
xt, nt = e.loc['treatment', 'conversions'], e.loc['treatment', 'visitors']
pc, pt = xc / nc, xt / nt
pp = (xc + xt) / (nc + nt)
se = np.sqrt(pp * (1 - pp) * (1 / nc + 1 / nt))
z = (pt - pc) / se
result = round(float(2 * (1 - stats.norm.cdf(abs(z)))), 4)

title: Bootstrap diff in means CI
task: With np.random.seed(3) and 2000 resamples, bootstrap mean(B) − mean(A) (resampling each group independently) and set result to the 2.5th percentile of the differences, rounded to 2 decimals.
hint: resample A and B separately each iteration.
answer:
np.random.seed(3)
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value'].to_numpy()
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value'].to_numpy()
diffs = [np.random.choice(B, len(B), True).mean() - np.random.choice(A, len(A), True).mean() for _ in range(2000)]
result = round(float(np.percentile(diffs, 2.5)), 2)

title: Permutation p-value
task: With np.random.seed(4), run a 2000-iteration permutation test of the difference in means (B − A): shuffle the combined values, split into sizes of B and A, and set result to the two-sided p-value = fraction of |permuted diff| >= |observed diff|, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
np.random.seed(4)
A = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'A', 'value'].to_numpy()
B = measurements.loc[measurements['group'] == 'B', 'value'].to_numpy()
obs = B.mean() - A.mean()
pool = np.concatenate([A, B]); nB = len(B)
count = 0
for _ in range(2000):
    np.random.shuffle(pool)
    d = pool[:nB].mean() - pool[nB:].mean()
    if abs(d) >= abs(obs):
        count += 1
result = round(count / 2000, 3)

title: Theoretical vs empirical
context: Compare a normal-fit quantile to the empirical one.
task: Set result to the absolute difference between the empirical 90th percentile of sample x and the 90th percentile of a normal fitted to x, rounded to 3 decimals.
hint: np.percentile vs stats.norm.ppf with fitted params.
answer:
x = sample['x']
mu, sd = stats.norm.fit(x)
emp = np.percentile(x, 90)
theo = stats.norm.ppf(0.90, mu, sd)
result = round(float(abs(emp - theo)), 3)

title: Two-predictor regression coefficient
context: OLS with numpy on before/after predicting a target.
task: Fit score ~ hours using numpy least squares with an intercept (design matrix [1, hours]) and set result to the fitted hours coefficient, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
X = np.column_stack([np.ones(len(regression)), regression['hours'].to_numpy()])
y = regression['score'].to_numpy()
beta = np.linalg.lstsq(X, y, rcond=None)[0]
result = round(float(beta[1]), 3)

title: Bayesian update
task: A test is 99% sensitive and 95% specific for a disease with 1% prevalence. Set result to P(disease | positive), rounded to 4 decimals.
answer:
sens, spec, prev = 0.99, 0.95, 0.01
pos = sens * prev + (1 - spec) * (1 - prev)
result = round(sens * prev / pos, 4)

title: Most influential point
task: Set result to the student id whose hours value is farthest from the mean hours (largest leverage proxy).
answer:
d = (regression['hours'] - regression['hours'].mean()).abs()
result = int(regression.loc[d.idxmax(), 'student'])

title: Point-biserial correlation
task: Set result to the point-biserial correlation between group (A=0, B=1) and value in measurements, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
g = (measurements['group'] == 'B').astype(int)
result = round(float(stats.pointbiserialr(g, measurements['value']).correlation), 3)

title: Empirical power
context: How often would we detect the effect?
task: With np.random.seed(6), simulate 1000 experiments: each draws n=40 from N(50,8) and n=40 from N(54,8), runs an independent t-test, and set result to the fraction with p < 0.05, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
np.random.seed(6)
hits = 0
for _ in range(1000):
    a = np.random.normal(50, 8, 40)
    b = np.random.normal(54, 8, 40)
    if stats.ttest_ind(b, a).pvalue < 0.05:
        hits += 1
result = round(hits / 1000, 3)

title: Exponential survival
task: For an exponential with rate 0.5 (scale 2), set result to P(X > 3), rounded to 4 decimals, using scipy.
answer: result = round(float(stats.expon.sf(3, scale=2)), 4)

answer: result = round(float(stats.percentileofscore(sample['x'], 185)), 1)

title: Regression significance

title: z vs t interval width gap
context: t is wider than z for small n.
task: For sample x, set result to the 95% t-CI width minus the 95% z-CI width (both using the sample SEM), rounded to 4 decimals.
answer:
x = sample['x']
n = len(x)
sem = x.std() / np.sqrt(n)
t_w = 2 * stats.t.ppf(0.975, n - 1) * sem
z_w = 2 * stats.norm.ppf(0.975) * sem
result = round(float(t_w - z_w), 4)

title: IQR outlier count
task: Set result to the number of sample x values outside [Q1 − 1.5·IQR, Q3 + 1.5·IQR] (an int).
answer:
x = sample['x']
q1, q3 = x.quantile(0.25), x.quantile(0.75)
iqr = q3 - q1
result = int(((x < q1 - 1.5 * iqr) | (x > q3 + 1.5 * iqr)).sum())

title: CI coverage check
context: Do 95% CIs contain the truth ~95% of the time?
task: With np.random.seed(7), run 1000 trials: draw n=30 from N(100,15), build a 95% t-CI for the mean, and set result to the fraction of CIs containing 100, rounded to 3 decimals.
answer:
np.random.seed(7)
hits = 0
for _ in range(1000):
    s = np.random.normal(100, 15, 30)
    lo, hi = stats.t.interval(0.95, 29, loc=s.mean(), scale=s.std(ddof=1) / np.sqrt(30))
    if lo <= 100 <= hi:
        hits += 1
result = round(hits / 1000, 3)
